why.text: Poor, light, well-drained soils on the Empordà plain give light, fresh, fruity wines with good acidity; old Garnacha is the classic liqueur wine.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also needle and sparkling wines, liqueur wines from Garnacha and Moscatel, and wines from overripe grapes.

soil.text: Poor, light, acid to neutral soils from conglomerates and sandstones, with good drainage.

why.text: Large temperature swings between day and night in this inland zone shape the alcohol, aromas and flavours of the wines.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also needle wines, sparkling wines and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Inland climate with a wide temperature range between day and night.

why.text: Altitude and distance from the sea give the wines their acid core, and wild herbs and forest add aromas of rosemary, lavender and thyme.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also needle wines, sparkling wines (a long local tradition) and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Temperature and rainfall differ from neighbouring areas; altitude, distance from the sea and the pre-coastal range give the wines acidity.

why.text: Well-drained granite soil with marine remains makes vines root deep and live under mild stress, which helps regulate yield.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also liqueur wines (rancio, mistela), natural sweet wines and traditional-method sparkling.

soil.text: Granite subsoil with marine remains, breaking into small grains at the surface; permeable.

why.text: Trepat, a grape native to Conca de Barberà, gives rosados and reds with their own character.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also liqueur wines, sparkling wines and needle wines.

why.text: Soil and climate bring white grapes to ripeness here, giving the whites freshness, acidity and fruit.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines, and sweet wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Warm, mild Mediterranean with much sun and about 500 mm of rain; many microclimates; a wide day-night gap in July and August.

why.text: Steep slopes with shallow slate soils and bedrock near the surface give wines high in dry extract and deep red colour.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, including single-estate (pago) wines; liqueur wines such as rancio, mistela and natural sweet.

climate.text: Mild and dry; the mountains cut off sea influence and shelter the zone from cold north winds; northwest winds blow.

soil.text: Very steep, shallow soils from slate, low in organic matter, with bedrock close to the surface.

why.text: Direct sea influence around Camp de Tarragona gives Mediterranean wines; continental Ribera d'Ebre gives fuller reds from Cariñena and Garnacha.

styles.text: Light whites, rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines such as mistela, moscatel and rancio.

climate.text: Direct sea influence in Camp de Tarragona; a continental influence in Ribera d'Ebre.

why.text: Mountains shelter the vines from the sea, giving hot days and cool nights; old Garnacha and Cariñena vines give full-bodied wines.

styles.text: Mainly reds, with whites and rosados; traditional liqueur wines and natural sweet wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean with some continentality: cold winters, hot dry summers, 500 to 600 mm of rain, mostly spring and autumn; strong day-night contrast.

soil.text: Three kinds: calcareous sedimentary soils, granitic sands (Falset) and slate «llicorella» that adds minerality.

why.text: Calcareous soils give the wines a salty note and long finish; Garnacha Blanca has a long tradition here.

styles.text: Whites (including single-variety Garnacha Blanca), rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean and southern in character, with harvests rich in sugar.
